questions.question: What equation defines the memoryless property?
questions.explanation: Memorylessness is the condition $P(X>s+t\mid X>s)=P(X>t)$ for all $s,t\ge0$: given survival to $s$, the chance of surviving $t$ more equals the fresh chance of surviving $t$.
questions.source_support: The definition states $P(X>s+t\mid X>s)=P(X>t)$ for all $s,t\ge0$.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
option_explanations: $P(X>s+t)=P(X>s)+P(X>t)$ is a false additivity claim; memorylessness is about the conditional probability.
$E[X\mid X>s]=0$ is false; the conditional mean equals the fresh mean.
$P(X=t)=P(X=s)$ for all $s,t$ is false; memorylessness concerns conditional survival.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
